historicalReferences: Velopark has been a proving ground for Brazilian motorsport talent for years. Many local drivers have honed their skills on this very Short Circuit.
This track has seen its fair share of dramatic moments, particularly in the lower formulas. The close proximity of the barriers on this short layout often leads to incidents.
While not a Formula 1 circuit, Velopark has hosted numerous national championships and touring car events, each leaving its mark on the track's history.
The tight confines of the Short Circuit have often led to strategic battles, with teams gambling on pit stops and tire choices to gain an advantage.
Many Brazilian motorsport legends have raced here at Velopark early in their careers. This track is a breeding ground for future stars.
This 2.2 km layout has seen some incredible late-braking moves over the years. It rewards bravery and precision in equal measure.
Velopark's Short Circuit has a reputation for producing unpredictable races. Safety cars are a common sight, bunching up the field and creating opportunities.
The atmosphere here is reminiscent of the glory days of Brazilian motorsport. Velopark keeps that passion alive.
We've seen some nail-biting championship deciders contested on this Short Circuit. The pressure is always immense.
The challenge of mastering this 7-turn layout has drawn some of the best drivers from South America and beyond to compete at Velopark.
cornerCallouts: They're approaching the first corner now, a tight right-hander that demands precision braking. A good exit is crucial for momentum.
Heading into Turn 2, another sharp right. This section is vital to get right for a good run down to Turn 3.
Turn 3 is a tricky left-hander that often catches drivers out. It's easy to run wide and lose time here.
Now the cars dive into Turn 4, a fast right-hand kink. It's all about maintaining minimum speed through here.
Through Turn 5, a sweeping left. The drivers will be using all the track here to maximize their corner speed.
Approaching Turn 6, a tight hairpin. This is a prime overtaking opportunity on the Short Circuit.
The final corner, Turn 7, is a fast right-hander that leads onto the main straight. Getting the power down early is key.
The run from Turn 7 down the main straight is deceptively long. Slipstreaming will be a major factor here.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this Short Circuit. The high lateral loads through the corners will punish the rubber.
With such a short lap, pit stops will need to be perfectly executed. Every second counts on this 2.2km layout.
Fuel consumption will be less of a concern on this circuit compared to longer tracks, but teams still need to manage their reserves effectively.
The pit window is relatively small here at Velopark. Timing the pit stop perfectly will be crucial for track position.
Teams will be carefully monitoring the weather radar. A sudden downpour could completely change the complexion of the race.
The short lap length means traffic will be a constant issue. Navigating through slower cars will be a key challenge.
With limited overtaking opportunities, qualifying position is even more critical on this tight and twisty circuit.
An early safety car could shake things up dramatically. Teams will need to be ready to react quickly to any unexpected events.
